 E M U F P H Z L R A X Y S D J K N G I V Q T B W C $ Which Row are these guys on? Well, doesn't matter for interval counts… O #57 > #47 #47 is 1st letter of K3 pt to encode #115(178) > ## 85/148 & ( 136/199 ) sqrt([ 178 ^2]*2) = 251.&c, encoder's interval for encoding K3 sqrt([ 136 ^2]*2) = 192.333, decoder's interval for decoding K3 My pet theory is that this is how the errors hint that one can encipher & decipher K3 (without even using the matrix & transposition). (.&c = ignore/drop decimal part of answer) Q3 > E3 (Third Query to third Error) = 158 sqrt([ 115 ^2]*2) = 162.&c sqrt([158^2]*2) = 223.&c F1 > Q2 (End of K1 to 2nd Query) = 162 F1 > Q3 (End of K1 to Query 3) = 223 Q3 > O1 (Query 3 to Omission 1) =162 Q2 > O1 (Query 2 to Omission 1) = 223 #256(319) is the midpoint of these two 162-length #256(319) is the midpoint of these two 223-length sections, which are separated by 61 characters. sections, which are overlapped by 61 characters. Or, of course, (162+223), or vice-versa, goes from the end of K1 to O1 without either gap or overlap. My extrapolation from my above pet theory is that the numbers and patterns immediately above ought also to be significant, presumably as hints at a K4 solution, since they cannot be seen until both K2 & K3 have been solved. I have not been able to come up with any application for them however, and invite consideration by the rest of you. - C. E.
